content.text:
Complete the provided drone sketch and turn it into a clearly recognizable agricultural spraying drone 
inspired by the DJI Agras series. Preserve all existing elements. Add four propellers, a camera, 
two landing legs, a central spray tank, spray boom, multiple spray nozzles, and visible spray output. 
Label all major components and add a title identifying the drawing as an agricultural spraying drone. 
Use the Excalidraw drawing tools to create the missing components. 
Align all the ellipses representing the propeller motor to the extending lines.
I'll help you complete the drone sketch. Let me first take a screenshot to see the current state of the Excalidraw canvas.

Let me analyze the current sketch. I can see:
- A central body (rounded rectangle) in the middle
- Four arms extending diagonally from the body
- Four gray circles (motors) at the end of each arm
- A yellow rounded rectangle at the bottom (likely for the spray tank or another element)

Let me read the page to understand the exact positions of existing elements.

To move canvas, hold mouse wheel or spacebar while dragging, or use the hand tool
Shapes
1
2
3
4
5
6
7
8
9
0
Canvas actions
100%

Let me look at the elements more carefully. The four gray circles are the motors, and I need to add propellers on them. Let me first understand the exact positions of the motor circles and arm endpoints.

Looking at the screenshot:
- Top-left motor: ~(392, 117)
- Top-right motor: ~(1007, 117)
- Bottom-left motor: ~(392, 447)
- Bottom-right motor: ~(1007, 447)
- Central body: ~(600-805, 235-330)
- Yellow rectangle: ~(555-850, 625-750)

Let me start by adding the propellers. I'll use the ellipse tool to draw propeller blades over each motor. First, let me select the ellipse tool.

The task mentions "Align all the ellipses representing the propeller motor to the extending lines." This means the motor ellipses should be aligned to the ends of the extending arm lines. Let me first zoom out a bit to have more room to work, then start building.

Let me begin by adding the four propellers. I'll use the ellipse tool to create propeller circles around each motor. Let me select the ellipse tool.

The ellipse tool is selected and I can see the properties panel. I notice the current motor circles are at the arm ends. Before drawing propellers, let me first address the task requirement to "Align all the ellipses representing the propeller motor to the extending lines."

Looking carefully at the arms:
- Top-left arm goes from body (~600, 240) to (~392, 117)
- Top-right arm goes from body (~805, 240) to (~1007, 117)
- Bottom-left arm goes from body (~600, 325) to (~392, 447)
- Bottom-right arm goes from body (~805, 325) to (~1007, 447)

The motors appear to be positioned at the line endpoints already. Now I'll draw the propellers. Propellers are large ellipses (circles) centered on each motor. Let me draw propeller circles around each motor.

First, let me set the stroke to a light blue/gray for the propellers and select a transparent background. Let me set the background to transparent first.

Now I've set stroke to blue and background to transparent. Let me draw the propeller circles. Propellers are wide flat ellipses. I'll draw each propeller centered on the motor. Let me draw the top-left propeller as an ellipse spanning around motor at (392, 117).

The top-left propeller ellipse is created, centered around the motor. This represents the propeller disc. Now let me draw the other three propellers. I'll select the ellipse tool again and draw each one.

All four propeller discs are now drawn as ellipses around each motor, aligned to the extending arm lines. Now let me add the spray tank. The yellow rounded rectangle at the bottom could be repurposed, but actually the task says to add a "central spray tank." 

Looking at the design, the DJI Agras drones have a central tank mounted under/on the body. The yellow rectangle at the bottom seems positioned to be the tank, but a central spray tank should be near the body. Let me interpret: I'll use the yellow rectangle as the spray tank and connect it. Actually, let me add a central spray tank on top of/within the central body area.

Let me think about the overall layout. I'll build:
- Central spray tank: I'll add a labeled tank in the center (the existing body can be the frame, tank inside)
- Spray boom: a horizontal bar below the body
- Spray nozzles: on the boom
- Spray output: dots/lines coming down from nozzles
- Camera: below the front of the body
- Landing legs: two legs going down

The yellow rectangle at the bottom is far from the body. Let me use it as the spray tank and position the boom below it, or I could reposition it. Actually, since we must "preserve all existing elements," I'll keep the yellow rectangle where it is and label it as the spray tank, then build the boom and nozzles below it.

Wait - but a "central spray tank" should be central. The yellow rectangle is roughly horizontally centered (555-850) which aligns with the body. It's just lower down. This works well as the tank mounted below the body. Let me connect the body to the tank and build the spray system below the tank.

Let me first add a camera below the front of the central body. I'll select the rectangle tool.

Rectangle tool is selected. Let me plan the layout. I'll add the camera as a small black rectangle below the front-center of the body. Let me set the stroke to black and background to a solid color first for the camera. Let me change stroke to black.
Now I'll draw the camera as a small rectangle below the front center of the body. The body bottom is around y=330. I'll place the camera at the front bottom center, around (680-720, 335-360).
The camera rectangle is placed below the front-center of the body. Now let me add a small lens circle inside the camera. Let me select the ellipse tool and draw a small circle in the camera.

Now let me add the two landing legs. Landing legs typically extend downward from the body. In the DJI Agras design, the legs form an inverted V or straight legs with feet. Let me use the line tool to draw the legs. I'll draw them going from the bottom of the body down and outward.

Let me select the line tool.

Now I'll draw the left landing leg. It should go from the bottom-left of the body down and outward. But wait - the bottom arms are already there going to the motors. The landing legs should be distinct, going down below the body. 

Let me think about the layout. The spray tank (yellow rectangle) is below the body. The landing legs need to reach the ground below everything. Let me draw the landing legs going from the tank/body area down. Actually, to make it clearly recognizable, I'll draw landing legs going down on either side, ending in horizontal feet at the bottom.

Let me set stroke width to bold first. Let me check the current tool panel.
The camera with lens is created. Now I have the line tool selected. Let me set the stroke width to bold for the landing legs to make them visible.

Now let me draw the landing legs. The legs should go down past the spray tank to form the ground support. The spray tank is at y=625-750. I'll draw legs that go from the body bottom down to below the tank level, forming the classic DJI Agras skid landing gear.

Let me draw the left landing leg. It goes from body bottom-left (~620, 330) down and slightly out to a foot at (~590, 620). I'll draw it as a multi-point line: vertical leg then horizontal foot. Let me click points for a multi-point line.

Left leg - going from (630, 330) down to (600, 560) then a foot. Let me draw the vertical part first as a single drag.
Now the right landing leg, from body bottom-right (~770, 330) down to (~805, 620).

The two landing legs are drawn going from the body down to the top of the yellow tank. Now I can see the landing legs connect the body to the tank area nicely. Now let me add feet to the landing legs. The feet are horizontal bars at the bottom of the legs. But the legs currently end at the tank top. 

Actually, looking at this, the legs end at y=620 which is the top of the tank. In a real DJI Agras, the legs go below the tank. Let me reconsider - the tank sits between the legs. This is actually a reasonable configuration where the legs bracket the tank. But for landing legs, they need feet to stand on. Let me extend the design so the tank is the spray tank and I'll add horizontal feet below.

Actually let me keep it cleaner: the legs go down alongside the tank. Let me add horizontal feet at the bottom. Let me draw two horizontal foot lines at the bottom of each leg. The left leg ends at ~(600, 620) and right at ~(805, 620). 

Let me add feet extending outward at the bottom of the legs. Left foot from (570, 620) to (620, 620), right foot from (785, 620) to (835, 620). Let me draw these below the tank actually - the tank bottom is at ~750. Let me reposition: I'll add feet at the tank bottom level to look like the drone stands on legs. 

Let me draw horizontal foot bars at y=755 (below tank). First left foot leg extension. Actually, let me just add horizontal feet at the leg ends for simplicity. Let me select line tool.

The landing legs now have horizontal feet at the bottom. The design is coming together nicely with the tank positioned between/behind the legs. 

Now I need to add the spray boom and nozzles. The spray boom is a horizontal bar that extends below the tank, and nozzles hang from it with spray output. Since the tank is at y=625-750, I'll place the spray boom below the tank at around y=770.

Let me draw the spray boom as a horizontal line below the tank. Let me select the line tool.

Now let me connect the tank to the spray boom with two short vertical connectors, and add nozzles. First let me add small vertical connectors from tank to boom. Actually, let me add the nozzles directly. Nozzles are small rectangles/shapes hanging below the boom. Let me add 4-5 nozzles along the boom.

Let me select the rectangle tool for nozzles and set background to a solid color.
I'll draw small nozzle rectangles hanging below the boom at 5 positions: x=550, 630, 700, 775, 855. Each nozzle is a small rectangle at y=768-785.

The spray boom with 5 nozzles is now created below the tank. Now I need to add the visible spray output - dots/spray coming down from each nozzle. Let me add spray output as small lines/dashes going down from each nozzle. 

Let me use the line tool with a lighter blue color and dotted style to represent spray. First let me select the line tool and change stroke to blue.
Now let me set the stroke width to thin and stroke style to dotted for spray effect.

Now let me draw the spray output as fanning-out dotted lines from each nozzle. For each nozzle I'll draw 2-3 diverging lines to simulate a spray cone. Let me draw spray from the first nozzle at x=550, y=785.

Nozzle 1 (~550): spray fanning to (535, 820) and (565, 820)

Excellent! The spray output (blue dotted lines fanning out from each nozzle) is now visible. The drone is taking great shape. Now I need to add all the labels and a title. 

Let me now add the text labels. First, let me select the text tool and set the color to black. Let me click on empty space first to deselect, then use the text tool.
Now let me add the title at the top. Let me click at the top center area to place the title text.

It seems clicking placed a text cursor but the panel shows text options. Wait, it seems the click at (500, 640) didn't create a text field, it just shows the text tool panel. Actually the message says "Double-click or press Enter to edit text" which means something got selected. Let me look - it seems my click didn't start typing. Let me instead click on the text tool again and then click on the canvas to place text for the title.

Let me place the title at the top of the drawing. I'll use the text tool.

I'll set font size to L (large) for labels first, but for the title I want XL which is already selected. Let me place the title. I'll click near the top of the canvas above the drone. But the top is around y=95. Let me place the title higher — actually there isn't much space above. Let me place the title in the upper-left empty area.

The title "Agricultural Spraying Drone" was placed but it's positioned to the right and got cut off (starts with "gricultural"). The text was placed starting at x=950 which pushes it off-screen. Let me click elsewhere to deselect, then move the title to a better centered position at the top.

Let me first click on empty space to finish editing.
The title is too big and off-position. Let me select it and move it. Let me use the selection tool and click on the title text to select it, then drag it to center it at the top.
The title is now selected. It's too large (XL) and extends off-screen. Let me first make it smaller by setting font size to L, then move it. Let me click the L font size.

The title now fits on screen at font size L. It reads "Agricultural Spraying Drone" and is fully visible. Now let me drag it to a better centered position at the top of the drawing. Let me drag it from its current position (~1130, 170) to the top center (~700, 100). Actually the top of the drone is at y~95, so let me place it above the whole drawing. Since there isn't much room at very top, let me move it up and to the center-left area above the body. 

Let me drag the title to position it centered above the drone body.

The title "Agricultural Spraying Drone" is now nicely centered at the top of the drawing. Now let me add labels for all the major components. I'll use smaller font (S or M) for labels. Let me add labels for:
1. Propeller (x4, but I'll label a couple)
2. Motor
3. Camera
4. Landing leg (x2)
5. Spray tank
6. Spray boom
7. Spray nozzle
8. Spray output
9. Central body / frame

Let me use the text tool with size S for labels. Let me select the text tool.
Now font size is S. Let me add the "Propeller" label near the top-left propeller. I'll place it above the top-left propeller area. Let me click at a spot near the top-left propeller.

"Propeller" label is placed above the top-left propeller. Now let me add the "Motor" label. The motors are the gray circles. Let me label the top-right motor. Let me select the text tool and click near the top-right motor.

Now let me add a "Propeller" label for the top-right one too, and label the other motors. Actually, to keep it clean, let me label one propeller and one motor which I've done. But the task says "Label all major components." Let me continue adding remaining labels: Camera, Landing leg, Spray tank, Spray boom, Spray nozzle, Spray output, and the central body/frame.

Let me add the "Camera" label. The camera is at (680-725, 335-365). Let me place a label pointing to it. I'll place it to the left of the camera with a line, but simpler to place text near it. Let me place "Camera" label below-left of camera.

I'll place the camera label to the left with an arrow. Actually let me just place text labels near each component. For camera, place it just below the camera box. But the legs are there. Let me place "Camera" label to the right of the camera at (740, 350).
